"Independent refereeing task for SoringP1 #301. Do NOT run another poset census and do NOT edit the repository, Lean files, or the board. Scratch only in /tmp. Your job is to audit or falsify a specific chain of claims that, if all correct, establishes T(6)=33 in the sense: every finite poset P with e(P) <= 33 has m(P) <= 6, and some poset with e(P) = 34 has m(P) = 7 (the staircase S_8).

Definitions: e(P) = number of linear extensions; m(P) = worst-case number of further comparisons to sort every linear extension of P, i.e. the exact minimax depth; \"universal element\" = an element comparable with every other element; \"core\" = finite poset with no universal element; \"ordinal sum\" A(+)B = A below B, no other comparisons; \"ordinal-indecomposable\" = not expressible as a nontrivial ordinal sum.

Claims to audit:
(C1) CORE REDUCTION: if x is comparable with every other element of P, then e(P) = e(P-x) and m(P) = m(P-x). Hence repeatedly deleting universal elements maps any P to a core C with e(C)=e(P), m(C)=m(P).
(C2) LEMMA: if P is an ordinal-indecomposable core with |P|>=4, then some maximal element x has P-x a core. Published proof sketch: assume every maximal deletion is non-core; take y_x universal in P-x, so y_x incomparable with x. If y_x is nonmaximal, take maximal w>y_x; then w is distinct from and incomparable with x; the witness y_w cannot equal x, so y_w<x; also y_x<w; y_x is universal in P-x so compares with y_w, and either order contradicts y_x incomparable with x or y_w incomparable with w. Hence all y_x are maximal; a core has at least two maxima; three maxima are impossible because the maximal witness would have to be comparable with a third maximum; with exactly two maxima the witnesses are reciprocal and every other element lies below both, giving P = (P-{x,w}) (+) {x,w}, a nontrivial ordinal sum. Contradiction.
(C3) DECOMPOSITION: if P = A(+)B is a core then A and B are cores; and |A|,|B| >= 2 (a one-element factor is universal).
(C4) SIZE BOUND: every core has e(P) >= |P|. Suggested induction following the generation structure (base 2-antichain e=2, 3-antichain e=6, one-relation-plus-isolated e=3; ordinal sums: e=eA*eB >= |A||B| >= |A|+|B| for |A|,|B|>=2; maximal insertion into a core A over a proper ideal I: e(P)=sum over L in Ext(A) of (|A|+1-p_L) where p_L = max position in L of I; I=empty gives (|A|+1)e(A); otherwise e(A) terms are each >=1 and, since A is a core, at least one term is >=2).
(C5) GENERATOR COMPLETENESS: these rules generate exactly all finite cores: base 2-antichain; maximal insertion of a new maximal element above any proper ideal of a generated core; ordinal sums of generated cores. Together with C4, iterating to level n<=E covers all cores with e<=E.

Deliver: for each claim, PROVED (with your own complete argument, not just agreement) / GAP (exact missing case) / FALSE (explicit counterexample with all relations, e and m computed exactly). Pay special attention to C2's assertion that the witness y_w cannot equal x, the case analysis when x is not maximal in P-w, and whether the two-maxima conclusion really yields an ordinal sum with P-{x,w} nonempty and 2-antichain top; and to C4's maximal-insertion inequality, including whether e(P) can equal |A| when |I| is nonempty. If every claim is correct, say so explicitly and state which part is most fragile. Report exact scripts/hashes only if you compute. Keep the final report under 900 words.
"
